newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Printronix Asian sales seen trebled by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Printronix Asian sales seen trebled by 2001.

text.p: U.S. computer printer maker Printronix Inc said on Tuesday it expected its sales to Asia to triple over the next five years.
Robert Kleist, president and chief executive officer, told reporters at a news conference he expected Asian sales to make up 30 percent of the firm's total revenues "in less than five years".
Sales in Asia currently account for under 10 percent of the company's total global turnover of US$159.3 million, he said.

But he said future growth would be driven by demand for its new generation of machines which print in the languages of the region such as Chinese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese as well as the languages of India.
China had strong potential and Printronix had several of the new generation machines on test in the market, Kleist said.
Kleist was speaking at the official opening of a new Singapore $16 million manufacturing plant of its Singapore subsidiary, Printronix AG.
The new factory brings the company's total investment in Singapore to S$35 million since it began operating here in 1985.

Printronix AG managing director, Philip Low, said the Singapore plant currently generated half of the company's global manufacturing output. This could rise to 70 percent in future, allowing the Irvine plant to concentrate efforts on research and development, he said.
Low said he expected the plant to help lift Printronix's global production to 10,000 printers per quarter from its current 8,000 units level.
Sales of Printronix's line matrix printers are split almost equally between own-brand products and those made for original equipment manufacturers, Kleist said.
Printronix revenues grew nine percent in fiscal 1996. Its revenues have recorded compound growth worldwide of about 16 percent a year over the last four years, said Kleist.
He said analysts were projecting 11 percent growth in revenues for the full year.
In addition to its sales to Asia, the Singapore plant also serves the European, African and Middle East markets.
